prompts.name: Correlation Visualization — Competitor Common Query
prompts.shortDesc: Visualize competitor relevance vs cost-to-outrank (Ahrefs/SEMrush export)
prompts.prompt:
You will build a correlation visualization from a Top Competing Domains export with columns: domain, competitor's keywords, common keywords, share, target's keywords, DR, traffic, traffic value, pages.

Meaning: common keywords = topical overlap (relevance); share = semantic proximity; traffic value = authority + cost-to-outrank signal (weight this most); DR = link-graph position. High DR + high share = expensive but highly relevant; low share + high traffic = different topical domain, lower priority. Low share means we need more pages.

Build an interactive HTML chart (Chart.js) with two Y-axes: a bar chart of common-keyword count per domain (left axis) and a line chart of traffic value per domain (right axis). Sort domains by traffic value descending, color-code by share (warm = high share, cool = low), add hover tooltips with all metrics, a legend, and a summary table below. Title it "Competitor Relevance & Cost-to-Outrank Dashboard". Export as a standalone HTML file.

prompts.name: Backlink Analysis & Visualization
prompts.shortDesc: Compare two sites' backlink quality with DR bins + traffic overlay

Compare the backlink profiles of two websites from their Referring Domains exports (columns include Domain, DR, Traffic).

Definitions: backlinks = authority via link-graph position; DR = domain popularity by link count; traffic = organic traffic of the linking domain. High DR + high traffic linking domain = high-quality backlink.

Use warm colors for site 1, cool colors for site 2. Title: "Backlink Quality Distribution Comparison"; X axis "DR Bin"; left Y "Number of Referring Domains"; right Y "Average Organic Traffic". Add a summary box (total backlinks, average DR, average traffic per site). Export as standalone HTML.

prompts.name: Heading Vectors Generator

prompts.name: Bulk SEO Post Generator (Koray-style → drafts)
prompts.shortDesc: Niche + keywords -> easy-read (grade-5) Koray-style posts drafted in bulk, with TL;DR + AI-ready FAQs
prompts.prompt: You are a Holistic / Semantic SEO content engine. From the niche and seed keywords below, research and produce a batch of complete, publish-ready articles, then save them ALL to the WordPress site as DRAFTS in one go using the bulk_publish_posts tool. Do the research yourself (use web search where available); do not ask me to supply it. NICHE + KEYWORDS: {{selected_text}} STEP 1 — Plan the cluster. Build a small topical map and choose the article titles to write (default 5 unless I gave a number). Each title targets a distinct search intent; avoid cannibalisation. Decide which posts should internally link to which (hub/spoke). STEP 2 — For EACH article, research and assemble: - entities: the real-world entities (people, orgs, products, places, concepts) Google associates with the topic; pick the most prominent. - secondary_keywords: LSI / semantically-related terms and n-grams to cover. - Heading vectors: H1 root, H2 short-form grouper questions, H3 condition/qualifier questions — a coherent contextual journey for answer-passage scoring. - content_html: the full body as clean HTML (h2/h3, p, ul, tables). One idea per sentence, short dependency trees, unique information gain (facts/data competitors lack). Embed 2-4 INTERNAL links (to the other posts in this batch or existing site pages) and 1-3 EXTERNAL authoritative links inline, with descriptive anchors. Include 1-3 references with descriptive alt text where they add value. Write for Generative Engine Optimisation: lead each section with a direct, quotable 40-60 word answer so AI engines can cite it. - key_takeaways: 3-5 short TL;DR bullets (see rules below). - meta_title (<=60 chars), meta_desc (<=155 chars), slug (kebab-case). - faqs: 3-5 {question, answer} pairs (becomes FAQPage schema + a visible block). - featured_image_url + featured_image_alt if you can supply a real, license-clear image URL; otherwise omit. - schema_type: BlogPosting by default (Article/NewsArticle if more fitting). Add custom_schema only when a richer type genuinely applies (e.g. HowTo, Product) as a valid JSON-LD object. - categories (names) and tags (names). READABILITY — write for a 5th-grade reader (this is mandatory): - Target Flesch Reading Ease 70-90 and Flesch-Kincaid grade 5 or under. The tool reports the score per post; if a draft comes back above grade 7, rewrite it simpler. - Sentences: average 8-14 words, hard cap ~20. One idea per sentence. - Paragraphs: 2-3 sentences max. Use short subheads often. - Words: prefer common, everyday words. Replace jargon, or define it in plain words the first time. Use 'use' not 'utilise', 'help' not 'facilitate'. - Voice: active and direct ('Turn off the router', not 'The router should be turned off'). Speak to the reader as 'you'. - Use bullet lists, numbered steps, and small tables to break up text. Bold the key phrase in important lines. - Lead every section with the answer in the first sentence, then explain. KEY TAKEAWAYS (for AI answer engines): - For each post supply key_takeaways: 3-5 short, self-contained bullet strings (each under ~20 words) that summarise the article's main answers. The tool renders these as a TL;DR box at the very top and marks them speakable for AI/voice engines. FAQs — optimise for BOTH classic and AI search engines: - 4-6 real questions people actually ask (pull from People-Also-Ask style intent). Use natural, conversational phrasing. - Each answer: lead with a direct 1-2 sentence answer (40-60 words, ~320 characters) so it can win a featured snippet AND be quoted verbatim by ChatGPT/Gemini/Perplexity; you may add one short follow-up sentence after. - Plain 5th-grade language. Put the most important fact first. Include the entity/keyword naturally in the answer. - These become FAQPage JSON-LD (for Google/Bing) and a visible Q&A block (which AI crawlers read). The article also gets SpeakableSpecification automatically. STEP 3 — Call bulk_publish_posts with posts = the array of article objects and default_status = 'draft'. Keep each content_html self-contained. Run bulk_publish_posts with dry_run=true FIRST, show me the plan (titles, slugs, intents, internal-link map), and on my confirmation run it again with dry_run=false. STEP 4 — Report a table of created drafts: title, slug, edit URL, word count, internal/external link counts, entities and FAQ counts. Note any posts that failed and why. Do not publish anything — leave everything as drafts for my review.

prompts.name: Readability Rewrite (5th-grade, AI-friendly)
prompts.shortDesc: Rewrite any article to an easy grade-5 reading level without losing meaning or SEO
prompts.prompt:
Rewrite the content below so a 5th-grade student can read it easily, WITHOUT losing accuracy, entities, keywords, or depth of information.

Rules:
- Target Flesch Reading Ease 70-90 and Flesch-Kincaid grade 5 or under.
- Sentences average 8-14 words, hard cap ~20; one idea per sentence.
- Paragraphs of 2-3 sentences. Add clear, frequent subheads (H2/H3 as short questions where it fits).
- Swap jargon for plain words, or define it simply the first time. Keep important named entities and keywords intact.
- Active voice; address the reader as 'you'. Lead each section with the answer, then explain.
- Turn dense passages into bullet lists, numbered steps, or small tables. Bold the key phrase in key lines.
- Keep every fact, statistic, and link. Do not invent new claims.

Deliver:
1. The rewritten article as clean HTML (h2/h3, p, ul, ol, table).
2. A short 'Key Takeaways' list (3-5 bullets) to place at the top for AI answer engines.
3. A before/after readability note: estimated grade level and reading ease, and what you simplified.
